visual_action: A split-screen video. The left side shows various clips of the Maui wildfires: trees whipping in the wind with fires in the background, burning buildings, people walking down a street as a building is engulfed in flames, and plumes of black smoke rising over a town. The right side shows clips of Donald Trump, Ron DeSantis, and Mike Pence speaking in different settings, such as at a podium or in an interview.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: Shown speaking on the right side of the screen, saying climate change is a "hoax" and that "it'll start getting cooler."

cast.name: Ron DeSantis
cast.evidence: Shown speaking on the right side of the screen, saying he has "always rejected the politicization of the weather."

cast.name: Mike Pence
cast.evidence: Shown speaking on the right side of the screen, stating that the climate is changing, but "not as dramatically as the radical environmentalists like to present."

cast.name: Republicans
cast.evidence: The on-screen text states, "Meanwhile, Republicans continue to downplay it:"

on_screen_text.text: Climate change helped fuel the fires in Maui. Meanwhile, Republicans continue to downplay it:
All of this with the global warming and —
a lot of it's a hoax.
There'll be modest changes in temperatures.
I wish science agreed with you.
Well I don't think science knows actually.

spoken_summary: The video compiles clips of Republican politicians downplaying climate change. Donald Trump calls global warming a "hoax" and predicts "it'll start getting cooler." Ron DeSantis says he rejects the "politicization of the weather." Mike Pence acknowledges climate change but claims it's "not as dramatically as the radical environmentalists like to present" and that there will be "modest changes." The video ends with Trump laughing at an off-screen person who says, "I wish science agreed with you," to which Trump replies, "Well I don't think science knows actually."
audio_music: A serious, ominous ambient track plays throughout. The music changes around the 8-second mark but maintains a somber and dramatic tone, meant to underscore the gravity of the fire footage and contrast it with the politicians' statements.
editing_pacing: The video uses a consistent split-screen format, cutting between different speakers and different scenes of the Maui fires. The pacing is a montage style with cuts every few seconds.
central_claim: Prominent Republicans like Donald Trump, Ron DeSantis, and Mike Pence are dangerously downplaying the threat of climate change, even as its effects, such as the Maui fires, cause real-world devastation.
intended_effect: To portray Republicans as out of touch and negligent on the issue of climate change, thereby generating opposition to their political positions and candidates.
